records.issue_text: The automatic guard in group_member.hbs resolves against the member item context instead of the group, so the remove link renders even for automatic groups and issues a DELETE that always fails with 422
records.rationale: group_member.hbs renders per-member via `itemView="group-member"` whose context is the member (Discourse.User), so `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves against the user, not the group model; members have no `automatic` property, so the remove link always renders, even for automatic groups, triggering a DELETE that the controller guards with `can_not_modify_automatic` (422). The diff clearly shows the itemView per-member template and the 422 guard, so the mechanism is verifiable.

records.issue_text: totalPages computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil
records.rationale: The diff adds `totalPages: Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. With user_count an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50), floor(2)+1 = 3 pages shown though only 2 exist, and `showingLast` (currentPage == totalPages) would never be true on page 2, enabling a 'next' click fetching an empty page. Math.ceil is the correct formula. Verified directly from the diff.
records.stripped_text: totalPages computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil

records.issue_text: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, producing an extra empty navigable page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil
records.rationale: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this yields 3 pages though only 2 exist, and since showingLast requires currentPage == totalPages, the UI will let users navigate to an empty last page and never mark the real last page as 'showingLast'. Math.ceil(user_count/limit) would be correct. This is verifiable directly in the diff.

records.issue_text: Unbounded limit parameter on groups members endpoint: params[:limit] has no upper clamp, allowing full materialization and serialization of entire group membership; previous 200 cap for automatic groups was removed (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb ~line 22)
records.rationale: The diff removes the previous cap logic (`limit = (params[:limit] || 200)` for automatic groups) and replaces it with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper clamp, so a client can pass an arbitrarily large limit and force serialization of an entire group's membership — a resource-exhaustion/DoS exposure introduced by this change.

records.issue_text: Unbounded limit parameter on public members endpoint in groups_controller.rb — no upper clamp allows clients to force serialization of the entire member list, a DoS/abuse surface (P3)
records.rationale: The diff shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` in the public groups_controller members action with no upper clamp, and this endpoint is now used to drive the admin UI pagination, so a client-controlled unbounded limit could force serialization of the entire member list. The mechanism (missing max clamp) is directly visible in the diff; whether it constitutes a material abuse surface vs. a hardening note is judgment, so moderate confidence.
